kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Borrowed from a Northwest Semitic language. In that language group the name was formed in reference to its tortuous course, on the example of Biblical Hebrew: לִוְיָה (liwyā́, “garland, wreath”) from לָוָה (lāwā́) = لَوَى (lawā, “to bend, to curve, to contort”) suffixed with ־תָּן (tān, forming agent nouns) → לִוְיָתָן (liwyāṯā́n, “leviathan, a mythological sea-serpent”). The same word up to the present Arabic form had the vowels contracted and the nisba ending added.
g: Litani (a river in Lebanon; an east-west river in South Lebanon north of Israel and south of the Zahrani)
